cards.text: Ezra tells this one himself, friend. He's a priest and a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, and King Artaxerxes of Persia just sent him to Jerusalem with silver and gold for God's house. Now Ezra writes down the family heads who came with him from Babylon.

Then comes the list of family heads and how many men came with each, including Hattush from the descendants of DAVID. One family head brings 28 men, another brings 300, and Ezra writes it all down like the most serious sign-up sheet in history.

Ezra gathers everybody at the canal that flows to Ahava, and they camp there three days. Then he walks the camp, searching among the people and the priests, like me counting sprinkles when something feels off.

cards.question: Ezra searches the camp by the Ahava canal. Which group can't he find a single one of?

cards.text: So Ezra sends a team of leaders and teachers to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia, and the name Elnathan shows up THREE times on that team. Somebody yells "Elnathan!" and three heads turn around.

cards.question: Ezra's team carries a message to Iddo and his kinsmen at Casiphia. What are they asked to bring back?

answers.text: Ministers for the house of God
Silver for the house of God

cards.text: And since the gracious hand of God is on them, the team doesn't come back empty. They come back with Levites. LEVITES, friend. Problem solved.

cards.question: First up is Sherebiah, from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi. Ezra calls him a man of ___.
True or false: Sherebiah's group of 18 men is the only group of Levites that comes.
They also bring 220 ___ servants, all designated by name. David and the officials had appointed them to assist the Levites.

cards.text: Now they've got their Levites, and the road to Jerusalem is waiting. But Ezra stops everything right there by the Ahava Canal.

cards.question: Ezra wants them to humble themselves before God and ask for a safe journey for their children and all their possessions. So what does he proclaim?

cards.text: Here's the thing. There are enemies on that road, and the easy move is to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen, but Ezra's too ashamed to ask.

cards.question: Why is Ezra ashamed to ask King Artaxerxes for an escort of soldiers?

answers.text: He told the king God is gracious to all who seek Him
The king had already turned down his other requests
He knew the king needed every soldier to guard Babylon

cards.text: Think about it. Telling the king "my God's got us" and then asking for spears is like telling your boss "I got this" and calling him from the parking lot for a ride, so instead they fast and petition their God about it.

cards.question: Ezra and the exiles fast and ask God for a safe journey. True or false: God grants their request.

cards.text: Next, Ezra sets apart twelve of the leading priests, plus Sherebiah, Hashabiah and ten of their brothers. He's got a job for them.

cards.question: What does Ezra weigh out into the hands of these priests and Levites?

answers.text: Silver and gold for God's house
Spears and shields for the road
Grain and oil for the altar

cards.text: We're talking 650 talents of silver, 100 talents of gold, 20 gold bowls, and two articles of fine polished bronze as precious as gold. Mother Miller bought me out of a bin for 25 cents, friend, so I know EXACTLY who the bargain is in this story.
Then Ezra looks at the priests and Levites and tells them, "You are holy to the LORD, and these articles are holy."

cards.question: True or false: Ezra says the silver and gold is tax money owed to the king.
Ezra gives the priests and Levites a job until they reach the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. What is it?

cards.text: So the priests and Levites take charge of it all, and on the twelfth day of the first month, they set out from the Ahava Canal. No soldiers. No horsemen. Just families walking toward Jerusalem with a FORTUNE in gold.

cards.question: Ezra's group heads for Jerusalem with no escort. What happens on the road?

answers.text: God protects them from enemies and bandits
Bandits steal part of the silver
The king's soldiers catch up to guard them

cards.question: They arrive in Jerusalem and rest there for ___ days.

cards.text: On the fourth day, in the house of God, they weigh it all out into the hand of Meremoth son of Uriah, the priest, with Eleazar son of Phinehas and two Levites beside him. Weighed at the canal, weighed AGAIN in Jerusalem, like me counting a fresh batch, taking three steps, and counting it again in case a cookie walked off.

cards.question: Everything is verified by ___ and ___, and the total is written down right then.

cards.text: Then the exiles who came back from captivity sacrifice burnt offerings to the God of Israel. Rams, lambs, the works.

cards.question: Part of the offering is bulls "for all Israel." How many bulls?
True or false: Along with the rams and lambs, the exiles bring a sin offering of 12 male goats.

cards.text: They also hand the king's edicts to the royal satraps and governors west of the Euphrates. Paperwork, delivered.

cards.question: Once the satraps and governors get King Artaxerxes's edicts, what do they do?

answers.text: Assist the people and the house of God
Demand tribute from the priests and Levites
Send Ezra and his group back to Babylon

cards.text: The gold's delivered and the offerings are made, but hang on, friend. Ezra's story in Jerusalem isn't done yet.
